title: Rabbi Shimon ben HaSegan
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: According to the Rambam in his Introduction to Zera’im, he was the son of Rabbi Chanina, the Deputy of the Kohanim.
He is mentioned three times in the Mishnah, and in all of them Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel speaks in his name:

In [Shekalim 8:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Shekalim.8.5): the curtain was a handbreadth thick. In [Ketubot 2:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Ketubot.2.8): one is raised to the priesthood on the testimony of one witness.
And in [Menachot 11:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Menachot.11.9): the baking of the showbread overrides a festival but not Yom Kippur.

In [Keritot 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.6b.1): “The leftover incense — once every sixty [years] — the words of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who said it in the name of the Segan”; Hyman suggests that perhaps it should read “in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben HaSegan.”

He is mentioned in [Tosefta Rosh Hashanah, chapter 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Rosh_Hashanah.2.7): “Shimon ben HaSegan says: If witnesses came from minchah time onward, they would sound the shofar.” And in [Tosefta Yoma, chapter 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Yoma.2.10): “Every day it had no nashtik (so it is in Zuckermandel’s Tosefta; see [Yoma 44b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.44b.16)), and on this day it had a nashtik — the words of Ben Segan.”[^1]
Seder HaDorot conjectures that he is [Shimon bar Kahana](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3424&lang=en).

notes.text: Keritot gives sixty or seventy years and attributes the teaching to “the Segan.” Hyman abbreviates the period and proposes Shimon ben HaSegan. The consulted Tosefta has the bracketed ושתיק; the Bavli reads ניאשתיק. The spelling נשתיק is Hyman’s report of Zuckermandel.
